Driver has following initialization sequence for Target mode
1. Driver initialization starts
2. ISP Abort is scheduled when the target is enabled.
qla2xxx [0000:04:00.0]-4807:25: ISP abort scheduled
qla2xxx [0000:04:00.0]-00af:25: Performing ISP error recovery - ha=ffff880caa9e0000.
3. DPC thread starts the ISP Abort
4. While DPC is resetting the chip and initializing the firmware
async events from the firmware about P2P mode
5. PRLI from a initiator is delivered to us followed by a PLOGI and then a
SCSI command which creates a session.
6. If the SCSI command is a WRITE in this case
column2: we issue XFR RDY and it

column1: gets dropped as can be seen with messages RESET-XFR because ISP Abort
is still active
qla2xxx [0000:04:00.0]-e902:25: RESET-XFR active/old-count/new-count = 1/1/1.
7. If the SCSI command is a READ
column2: we issue RESPONSE and they get dropped

column1: as well because Abort is still active.
qla2xxx [0000:04:00.0]-e901:25: RESET-RSP active/old-count/new-count = 1/1/1
8. Now eventually
column2: ISP Abort finishes clearing the DPC flags.

column1: qla2xxx [0000:04:00.0]-8822:25: qla2x00_abort_isp succeeded.
qla2xxx [0000:04:00.0]-4808:25: ISP abort end.
9. Since we dropped SCSI commands silently (without any responses sent
to the initiator) initiator waits for a SCSI timeout (which is 60
seconds in our case)
column2: Sends an ABTS which fails since there

column1: no se_cmd found for the tag that ABTS is referencing as the
commands were cleaned up in Step 6 and 7.
10. Initiator send an IO after the ABTS which succeed fine.
To fix the above case
column2: the following changes have been made:

column1: - To prevent target from dropping commands silently
instead to check for an active chip reset. Once the port is online during
a chip reset phase
column2: we are good to process the commands.

column1: - Clean up qla2x00_restart_isp to not set the online flag and process ATIO
as it is unnecessary. During a chip reset
after setting the online flag to 1
column2: so ATIO's won't be missed and hence

column1: no need to process ATIO's after setting the online flag.
